lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Replace the example-style profile link if it is not a placeholder, and check that the contact details are application-ready.
items.because: The link may not be your actual professional profile URL.

items.says: Put the 2024 internship above the 2018–2023 role.
items.because: The current order is not reverse chronological and makes the timeline harder to scan.

items.says: Consider leading with Experience rather than Education for roles that prioritize work history.
Make the target role and career transition clear.
items.because: The move from operations to product and then to diesel mechanic may prompt questions for PM roles.

items.says: Standardize date and location formatting across entries.
items.because: Consistency makes the timeline easier to compare.

items.says: Make the recent mechanic role’s relevance to the target role clear.
items.because: It makes the career story less immediately clear for a PM application.

items.says: Clarify what “under 5 days per job” measures and over what period.
items.because: The turnaround figure’s scope is unclear.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the team’s.
items.because: Attribution for the fleet work and turnaround figure is unclear.

items.says: Add a substantiated result or reconsider the bullet’s space on a PM-focused résumé.
items.because: It describes responsibilities but not their significance.

items.says: Specify what you owned beyond the scorecards and meeting, and what changed as a result.
items.because: “Owned” and “discussed them” do not show an effect on decisions or outcomes.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period, calculation, and whether the 30% reduction was sustained.
items.because: Those details make the metric easier to trust.

items.says: Define forecast error and explain how the before-and-after figures were calculated.
items.because: Readers need to know the metric is comparable across periods.

items.says: Separate the rollout’s scope from your personal ownership.
items.because: The bullet combines rollout, SOP changes, training, negotiations, and savings.

items.says: Explain how the 1,800 driver hours were measured or estimated.
items.because: The annual savings figure needs a clear basis.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period and calculation of median time to first payment.
Clarify the pilot’s merchant count, region, and whether the change applied to all those merchants.
items.because: The pilot scope is ambiguous.

items.says: Describe the conversion lift as 5 percentage points, not a 5% increase.
items.because: The figures move from 61% to 66%.

items.says: Clarify whether “all merchants” means the pilot region or the whole business.
items.because: The rollout scope is unclear.

items.says: Explain the full RICE method and how it informed roadmap prioritization, or reconsider the bullet.
items.because: One scoring input does not show how you prioritized the roadmap.

items.says: Clarify the Reach proxy of support tickets a feature would close.
items.because: It may be read as a different kind of impact measure.

items.says: Identify the distinct decision or deliverable this work produced.
items.because: It overlaps with the RICE and leadership-presentation bullets.

items.says: Make the outcome clearer instead of listing so many activities.
items.because: The long list obscures the outcome.

items.says: The checkout experiment appears to be presented twice.
items.because: The earlier conversion bullet describes the same test.

items.says: Clarify what the reported effect was measured on and how it was validated.
items.because: The experiment’s scope is unclear.

items.says: Make the connection between the presented results and funded rollout clear.
items.because: The bullet overlaps with the onboarding result and roadmap work.

items.says: Clarify the rollout scope alongside the claim that the flow was already shipped to all merchants.
items.because: The two claims may conflict.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students were eligible or actual users.
items.because: “Launched to” does not establish the app’s reach.

items.says: Explain how the nine tonnes of rescued food were measured.
Make sure “launched” reflects the app’s real deployment status.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Give the weekly-active-user measurement period.
Avoid attributing the whole increase to reminders without support for that causal link.
The move from 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
Clarify the fill-rate time period and definition.
Explain the link between the volunteer shift system and the fill-rate result if it can be substantiated.
Keep modeled potential savings distinct from realized savings.
items.because: Funding a pilot does not establish that the savings were achieved.

items.says: Use active wording and specify your contribution.
items.because: The passive wording does not make your role clear.

items.says: Explain what “adopted” means in practice and, if possible, show a concrete result.
items.because: The bullet may be less useful without a concrete result.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome is counted twice.
items.because: The first practicum bullet already reports that the client funded a pilot.

items.says: Include distinct evidence of your analysis, recommendation, or role only if it adds something separate.
items.because: The approval repeats the first bullet’s outcome.

items.says: Show more depth and keep only product skills you can discuss concretely.
items.because: The skills are broad, and the list does not show depth.

items.says: Consider adding tools you actually used and can explain.
items.because: The tools list is short.
